mil3.3.3:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say ‘no first point is found’, what is that first point?”
mil3.3.3:1.3: “Great King, the past time is the first point.”
mil3.3.3:1.4: “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say ‘no first point is found’, venerable sir, is every first point not found?”
mil3.3.3:1.5: “Some are found, Great King, and some are not found.”
mil3.3.3:1.6: “Which, venerable sir, are found, and which are not found?”
mil3.3.3:1.7: “Great King, the idea that before this there was no ignorance at all, in every way, completely—such a first point is not found. What comes to be having not been, and having been passes away—this first point is found.”
mil3.3.3:2.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, what comes to be having not been, and having been passes away—does that not go to its end cut off at both ends?”
mil3.3.3:2.2: “If, Great King, it goes to its end cut off at both ends, can what is cut off at both ends be made to grow?”
mil3.3.3:2.4: “Venerable sir, I am not asking this: can it be made to grow from a first point?”
mil3.3.3:3.2: The elder gave him the simile of a tree: “And the aggregates are the seeds of the entire mass of suffering.”
